title.value: Any2Policy: Learning Visuomotor Policy with Any-Modality
title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly stated at the beginning of the document as 'Any2Policy: Learning Visuomotor Policy with Any-Modality.'
title.quote: Any2Policy: Learning Visuomotor Policy with Any-Modality

analysis.description: The paper presents an end-to-end general-purpose multi-modal system designed for robots, named Any2Policy, which enables them to handle tasks using various modalities such as texts, images, sounds, and more. This versatile functionality aims to create more generalizable embodied agents. A new dataset with 30 diverse robotic tasks across multiple modalities has been introduced to benchmark this system.

type.justification: The paper includes experiments using several simulation benchmarks and real-world settings to validate the proposed multi-modal embodied agent system, indicating it is empirical research that focuses on experimental evidence.
type.quote: We conducted extensive validation of our proposed unified modality embodied agent using several simulation benchmarks, including Franka Kitchen and Maniskill2, as well as in our real-world settings.

name.justification: The research focuses on developing a multi-modal embodied agent for robots, which aligns with the field of Robotics.
name.quote: Addressing this limitation, we present an end-to-end general-purpose multi-modal system named Any-to-Policy Embodied Agents.

name.justification: The study emphasizes on leveraging the power of multi-modal inputs like text, audio, image, and point cloud for embodied agents, making Multi-Modal Learning a key subfield.
name.quote: Our innovative approach involves training a versatile modality network that adapts to various inputs and connects with policy networks for effective control.

name.justification: The paper involves extracting features from multiple modalities for representation in policy learning, falling under Representation Learning.
name.quote: These features are then transformed into standardized token representations, ensuring uniformity at the neural network level via projection layers.

name.justification: The use of image and video modalities to provide visual input and observation within the Any2Policy system aligns with Computer Vision.
name.quote: Our dataset, RoboAny, stands out as the first to support a comprehensive range of modalities in robotics.

name.justification: The main model discussed and proposed in this paper is the Any2Policy model, designed for unified multi-modal embodied agents.
name.quote: Our method, referred to as Any-to-Policy Robot Model (abbreviated as Any2Policy), is illustrated in Figure 1.

is_contributed.justification: The paper introduces the Any2Policy model as a contribution for handling multi-modal inputs in robotic systems.
is_contributed.quote: We introduce any-to-policy models that enable a unified embodied agent to process various combinations of modalities.

is_executed.justification: Experiments were conducted in both simulation and real-world settings, indicating that the model was implemented and executed.
is_executed.quote: We conducted extensive validation of our proposed unified modality embodied agent using several simulation benchmarks, including Franka Kitchen and Maniskill2, as well as in our real-world settings.

is_compared.justification: The paper contains experimental comparisons between Any2Policy and other modality-specific models and SOTA models like VIMA and R3M.
is_compared.quote: We compare Any2Policy with modality-specific approaches in Table 1.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper does not reference a previous specific model paper, as Any2Policy is an original contribution of this paper.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Our method, referred to as Any-to-Policy Robot Model (abbreviated as Any2Policy), is illustrated in Figure 1.

name.justification: The dataset introduced in the paper is named RoboAny, designed for evaluating multi-modal robotic tasks.
name.quote: Our dataset, RoboAny, stands out as the first to support a comprehensive range of modalities in robotics.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The dataset is a new contribution and thus does not have a referenced paper title.
referenced_paper_title.quote: In support of this project, we are releasing a substantial real-world dataset consisting of 30 tasks, where each task includes 30 trajectories, all annotated with multi-modal instructions and observations, mirroring the setup used in our experiments.

name.justification: Franka Kitchen is one of the simulation benchmarks utilized in this study for evaluation purposes of the Any2Policy framework.
name.quote: Our experiments showcase the promising capability of building embodied agents that can adapt to diverse multi-modal in a unified framework.
